'''Arabana''' or '''Arabuna''' {{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʌr|ə|b|ʌ|n|ə}}<ref>Laurie Bauer, 2007, ''The Linguistics Student’s Handbook'', Edinburgh</ref> is an [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]] of the [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan family]], spoken by the [[Wongkanguru]] and [[Arabana people]].

The language is in steep decline, with an estimated 250 speakers according to 2004 NILS, to just 21 speakers found in the 2006 census.<ref name=AIATSIS/>

== Geographic distribution ==
Arabana is spoken at [[Neales River]] on the west side of [[Lake Eyre]] west to the [[Stuart Range, South Australia|Stuart Range]]; [[Macumba River|Macumba Creek]] south to [[Coward Springs]]; at [[Oodnadatta]], [[Lora Creek]], [[Lake Cadibarrawirracanna]], and [[Oodnadatta Track|The Peake]]. Their boundary with the [[Kokatha|Kokatha people]] to their west is marked by the margin of the scarp of the western tableland near [[Coober Pedy]].<ref name=AIATSIS/>

==Dialects==

Arabana has three dialects: Piltapalta, which [[Luise Hercus|Hercus]] refers to as "Arabana Proper", Wangkakupa, and Midhaliri.<ref name=AIATSIS/> [[Wangganguru dialect|Wangganguru]] was also considered a dialect.

==Phonology==
